Every subsequent open re-walks and diffs against that baseline, rendering three groups — added, removed, changed — with byte deltas and a per-file line-level diff computed in the browser from the stored text. A 'set new baseline' button re-snapshots with a confirm, and the header shows how old the current baseline is. Explicitly labels itself as tracking since the baseline, not since a commit.
why: The API has no mtime, so this is only possible because a canvas persists — the card's memory IS the feature, and the same idea inline would be impossible. It is the question you have after the agent has been editing for twenty minutes: what did it actually touch.

prompt: 帮我看看 src/client/runtime 里的 import 关系
sketch: Walks the directory, reads every .ts/.tsx, extracts import specifiers by scanning source (static imports, `export ... from`, dynamic `import()`), resolves relative paths and the `$dsh/*` and bare-specifier cases into buckets, and draws a dependency graph as an SVG force-free layered layout — layer by topological depth, so the leaves sit at the bottom. Cycles are highlighted in the error colour with the cycle path listed underneath. Clicking a node isolates its in- and out-edges; a side list shows orphans (nothing imports them) and hubs, ranked.
why: An import graph is the shape of the code, and you normally need a bundler or madge to see it. Orphans and cycles are the two findings that change what you do next. Canvas because you refer back to it repeatedly while refactoring.

prompt: 这两个目录有啥不一样
sketch: Two path inputs at the top (pre-filled from the message), both walked recursively, and a merged union listing every relative path with a status: only-in-left, only-in-right, same, or differing. Differing rows expand into a side-by-side line diff read at click time. A summary strip counts each bucket. Same-content-different-size is impossible so equality is checked by full text compare for text files and by size for anything that fails to read. Swapping sides is one button.
why: `diff -r` with no diff, and it is the exact question when you have a template dir and a generated dir, or two similar packages. Canvas because comparing is an activity, not a lookup — you drill into file after file.

prompt: 我的 .env 里都配了些啥
sketch: Parses .env (and .env.local / .env.example if present) into rows of key, value, and source file. Every value renders masked by default as the first two characters plus dots plus the length; a per-row eye toggles one value, never all at once, and the reveal resets when the canvas is reopened. A fourth column cross-checks against .env.example and flags keys that the example declares but the real file lacks, and keys set in .env with no counterpart. Values are editable in place; committing re-reads the file, verifies it matches what was parsed on mount, rewrites only the changed lines preserving comments and ordering, and shows the resulting file text in a confirm step before writing. In a read-only session the fields render disabled with the sandbox refusal named in the footer.
why: Secrets are exactly the thing you must not paste into a chat transcript to look at, so a card that shows them in place, masked, is strictly safer than asking the agent. The write path is safe because it re-reads and compares before committing, preserves comments rather than regenerating the file, and shows final text — three separate guards against clobbering.

prompt: package.json 的 scripts 我想改一下
sketch: A structured editor over one JSON file: keys on the left, editable values on the right, add/remove rows, with the raw JSON preview updating live beside it. Validates as you type — duplicate keys, invalid JSON in nested values, trailing-comma paste — and the commit button stays disabled with the reason shown while anything is invalid. Committing re-reads the file, compares the on-disk text with the text parsed on mount, and if it drifted it refuses and offers to reload rather than overwrite. Serialization preserves the original indentation and key order, appending new keys at the end, so the resulting diff is minimal.
why: Editing JSON by hand is where you break a build with a comma. Safety is concrete here: validation gates the button, the drift check makes the concurrent-agent race a refusal instead of a silent clobber, and preserving indent/order means the write produces a one-line diff instead of a reformat.

prompt: 给我搭一个新的 canvas 骨架
sketch: A scaffolding form: canvas id, title, which of $dsh/fs, $dsh/ai, $dsh/chat it should import, whether it needs a sub-directory for components, whether it persists to localStorage. Below the form, a file manifest — every path that will be created, with the full generated content viewable per file in tabs. Before writing, each target path is probed with readFile and any that already exists is flagged in the error colour with its checkbox forced off, so scaffolding can never overwrite. Writing happens file by file with a live per-row status (pending / written / failed), and a failure stops the run and reports which files already landed.
why: Scaffolding is the classic thing you shell a generator for, and here there is no shell. Safe because it shows the complete manifest first, refuses existing paths outright rather than asking, and writes serially with per-file status so a partial run is legible instead of leaving you guessing what got created.

prompt: 这些截图文件名太乱了 帮我批量重命名
sketch: Pick a directory, see its files, and define a rename with a find/replace pair (literal or regex) plus optional sequential numbering with a pad width. The table shows old name → new name for every file, live, with collisions and no-op rows flagged; unaffected files grey out. Because the API has no rename or delete, the card is explicit about what it does: it writes the new filenames with the original content, shows a running count, and then — for cleanup — offers a single sendMessage that asks the agent to delete the specific old paths it just duplicated, listing them. Nothing is written until the preview has zero collisions and you confirm.
why: Batch rename is the canonical terminal task and the preview table is the entire safety story — you see every resulting name before anything happens. It is also the most honest card in the set about an API limit: rather than pretending to rename, it does the half it can and hands the deletions to the agent, which is what $dsh/chat is for.

prompt: tsconfig 里的路径别名到底指到哪
sketch: Reads tsconfig.json (following `extends` up the chain), lists every `paths` alias with its baseUrl-resolved target, and then verifies each one: probes the target with readdir or readFile and marks it resolved or dangling. An input at the bottom takes an arbitrary import specifier and shows the resolution walk — which alias pattern matched, what the substitution produced, whether that file exists, and which extension candidate won.
why: 'Why does @/foo not resolve' is a pure terminal-adjacent question, and the answer is usually a stale alias pointing at a moved directory. Probing turns config into verified fact. Inline because you ask it once when something is broken.

prompt: 我这项目里配置文件是不是有冲突的
sketch: Hunts for the known config families across the tree — tsconfig variants, eslint/oxlint, prettier/oxfmt, package manager lockfiles, .nvmrc vs engines, multiple .env layers — and renders one row per family. Each row shows every file found, and where two sources declare the same setting differently it shows both values side by side with the one that actually wins marked, plus a sentence on the precedence rule. Lockfile row flags the case where more than one manager's lockfile exists. Each finding has a 'fix this' button that sendMessages a precise description of the conflict to the agent.
why: Config drift is invisible until it wastes an afternoon, and it is only detectable by someone standing in the directory. The sendMessage buttons close the loop: the card finds it, the agent fixes it, and you never typed the file path.

prompt: 刚才那个改动我想看看到底改了啥
sketch: Reads the file the agent just touched and diffs it against the pre-edit text held in the card's own snapshot — if none exists, it diffs against the nearest .orig/.bak or falls back to showing the file with a note that no baseline exists. Rendered as a unified diff with syntax-tinted added/removed lines using the success and error variables, collapsed context between hunks expandable, and a per-hunk line count. A header states plainly which baseline it is diffing against, so it can never imply it is showing a git diff when it is not.
why: The gap between what you think the agent did and what it did. The design constraint I care about is the honesty of the baseline label — with no git available, a diff card that implies git is actively misleading.

prompt: 这个 yml 配置里的字段都啥意思
sketch: Reads the config file, renders it as an outline tree of keys with values, and lets you click any key to get an explanation streamed from $dsh/ai — the card sends the key path, the surrounding block, and the filename as context, and streams the answer into a panel beside the tree. Explanations are cached per key path in localStorage so re-clicking is instant and a reopened canvas keeps what you already learned. Keys you have explained get a small dot so you can see your reading progress through an unfamiliar file.
why: This is where $dsh/ai is genuinely warranted by the plugin's own test: the set of config keys in the world is open, so no fixed table could cover it. The cache is what makes it feel like a document rather than a chat — and it is 'either' because a quick one-key question is inline while learning a whole unfamiliar config is a canvas.

prompt: 帮我看看哪些文件特别大 该拆了
sketch: Walks the tree, uses the size field from readdir (no re-read needed for the ranking, so it is fast), and renders the top files as a horizontal bar chart with a size axis. For source files it additionally reads the top ~20 and shows line count and, where the language allows, a crude export/function count so 'large' distinguishes a 2000-line god module from a large generated blob. A minimum-size slider and an extension filter narrow it. Rows have a button that sendMessages a request to split that specific file.
why: Uses the one piece of metadata the API actually gives you, and it is the classic 'where is the rot' question you ask standing in a repo. Distinguishing generated bulk from real complexity is what keeps it from being a useless du.

prompt: 这个测试文件里都测了些啥
sketch: Reads a test file and extracts the describe/it/test structure by scanning source, rendering it as an indented outline of the test names — the spec as prose. Skipped and only-marked cases are flagged in the warn colour with a count at the top, since a stray `.only` is the bug that makes a green run meaningless. Each leaf expands to show its body. A header states clearly that nothing was executed and these are the declared cases, not results.
why: With no test runner available, the honest thing is to show the spec, not fake results — and the `.only` detection is a real find that costs nothing. The disclaimer is load-bearing: a card that looked like a test report while running nothing would be the worst possible card here.

prompt: 我想把这次的改动写个 commit message
sketch: Reads the files it can identify as changed (from a stored baseline if one exists, otherwise from an explicit path list you paste or pick), assembles a compact diff summary, and streams a conventional-commit message from $dsh/ai with the diff as context. Type and scope are editable dropdowns that re-generate, and there is a regenerate button for a different phrasing. The result sits in a copy-ready block, and a second button sendMessages the message to the agent so it can run the commit itself, since the card cannot.
why: Uses all three capabilities in the one place where each is genuinely needed — files for the evidence, the model because phrasing is open-ended, and chat because committing is a shell action the card provably cannot perform. Editable type/scope beats a single take you have to retype.

prompt: 为啥 for 循环里 setTimeout 打出来的都是 3 啊
sketch: 左边一列三个 setTimeout 的闭包盒子，中间一个大方框标着 i。顶上一个开关：var / let。开关在 var 时，三个盒子的箭头全指向同一个 i 方框；点「跑一步」，i 从 0 变 1 变 2 变 3，三条箭头指向的数字同步跟着变，最后定时器触发时三个都读到 3。拨到 let，方框立刻裂成三个独立的 i₀ i₁ i₂，每个盒子各自连一个，再跑一遍就打出 0 1 2。用户拖「循环次数」滑块 3→6 时盒子和箭头实时增减。
why: 这是最经典的一次性困惑，答完就走，inline 正好待在提问旁边。核心不是「解释闭包」而是让人亲手把 var 拨成 let，看见一个方框裂成三个——这个「裂开」的动作就是概念本身。不需要任何能力，纯 React 状态机。

prompt: 事件循环到底啥顺序，我 setTimeout 和 Promise 混着写就晕
sketch: 上方一个可编辑的代码列表（预置几行：console.log、setTimeout、Promise.then、await），每行左边有个「▶ 排队」按钮。下面三条泳道：调用栈、微任务队列、宏任务队列，右边是输出区。用户点「单步」，一帧只做一件事：栈弹出一项 → 该项产生的回调飞进对应队列 → 栈空时微任务队列整队清空（逐个飞出）→ 才轮到一个宏任务。用户可以拖动代码行改顺序，输出区立刻重算。
why: 事件循环的规则「微任务队列必须清空才取一个宏任务」用文字说十遍不如让人点十下单步看队列排空。canvas 因为这是要反复回来试不同代码顺序的，localStorage 存住用户自己编排的那几行。不能真跑代码（没 shell），所以是对固定几种语句的模型模拟，诚实地只支持这几类。

prompt: 帮我看看我这个 CSS 里的选择器优先级都算多少
sketch: 读取用户指定的 .css 文件，把每条规则列成一行，右边显示 (a,b,c) 三段权重条——id 数、class/属性/伪类数、元素数，条的长度就是权重。顶部一个输入框让用户敲一个元素（如 div.card#main:hover），所有能命中它的规则高亮并按权重排序堆叠，最上面那条标「胜出」。用户往输入框里加一个 class，堆叠顺序当场重排。还能拖某条规则上的 !important 徽章开关，看它如何直接跳到顶。
why: 特异性是选择器字符串的纯函数，浏览器里可以完全正确地算出来，不需要执行任何东西——这是 fs 唯一诚实的用法。价值全在「是我自己的 CSS」而不是教科书例子。canvas 因为调样式是持续几天的事，用户会反复打开它。

prompt: flex-grow flex-shrink flex-basis 三个到底谁管啥
sketch: 一个容器里三个彩色 item，容器右边缘有个粗拖柄，用户左右拖就是在改容器宽度。每个 item 下面三个数字步进器：grow / shrink / basis。拖窄容器时 shrink 大的那个明显瘪得快，拖宽时 grow 大的吃掉全部剩余空间。item 上实时叠一行小字显示当前实际宽度和「剩余空间 × grow/总grow」的算式。把 basis 从 auto 改成 0，三个 item 的比例立刻从「按内容」变成「纯按 grow」。
why: flex 的三个属性只有在容器宽度变化时才显出区别，所以「拖容器边缘」这个动作必须是主操作，而不是改数字。算式随拖动实时更新，把感觉和公式钉在一起。canvas 给的 320-720px 面板本身就是可变宽的，很搭。

prompt: 我这个正则老是匹配不上，能有个地方让我边改边看吗
sketch: 上面是正则输入框和 flags 勾选，中间是多行测试文本区，匹配段落实时高亮、捕获组用不同底色并在右侧列成表格。下面一条「引擎足迹」时间轴：拖动滑块可以逐步回放引擎在某个位置的尝试与回溯，当前尝试的字符在文本里闪红。旁边一个「生成一批测试串」按钮，把当前正则丢给模型要十条应该命中/不该命中的样例，直接填进测试区。
why: 正则是最典型的「改一个字符结果全变」，必须常驻——canvas + localStorage 意味着明天回来正则和测试文本都还在。ai 只用在生成测试语料这一件生成型小事上，单轮足够；解释留给上面的聊天回复，卡片不重复啰嗦。

prompt: git 的 commit / tree / blob 到底是啥关系
sketch: 左边一个假的工作区文件列表，用户可以点文件改内容、点「暂存」、点「提交」。右边同步长出对象图：blob 方块（内容哈希）、tree 圆角框、commit 菱形带 parent 箭头。改一个文件再提交，新 commit 只新增一个 blob 和路径上的 tree，其余节点用虚线标「复用」。拖动分支标签 HEAD 到旧 commit，右边整图变灰只剩可达部分。
why: git 的核心洞察是「树是不可变的、改一个文件只重建一条路径」，这个只有在用户自己提交第二次、看见大部分节点标成『复用』时才会真的懂。不能真跑 git（无 shell），所以是自带的小型对象模型模拟，操作对象是卡片里的假仓库，诚实且完整。canvas 因为要连着提交好几次才有意思。

prompt: 跨域这块我一直没搞明白，预检请求啥时候会发
sketch: 左边一个请求构造器：方法下拉、URL 域名输入、几个可增删的自定义 header、Content-Type 下拉、withCredentials 开关。右边是时序图：浏览器 → 服务器。一旦某项越过「简单请求」边界（比如 header 加了 X-Token，或 Content-Type 改成 application/json），时序图上方立刻多出一段 OPTIONS 预检泳道，并把触发它的那一项高亮标红。下面是服务器响应头编辑区，用户删掉 Access-Control-Allow-Headers 里的一项，时序图上预检那步就变成红叉并显示浏览器控制台会打的那句原话。
why: CORS 的痛点是「我不知道是哪一项让它变复杂的」。让用户逐项加 header、看预检泳道凭空出现，就是把规则变成了因果反馈。响应头也可编辑，才能演出失败那一半——只演成功路径的教学卡片是没用的。

sketch: 一个 64 格的位条：1 位符号、11 位指数、52 位尾数，用户可以直接点任意一格翻转 0/1，上方的十进制值实时变。预填 0.1 和 0.2 两条，中间显示它们各自真正的精确十进制展开（0.1000000000000000055511…），下面第三条是相加结果，把与 0.3 不同的那几位标红。旁边一个滑块「假装尾数只有 N 位」，从 52 拖到 8，误差被放大到肉眼可见。
why: 点位翻转是唯一能让人感到『这些格子就是这个数的全部』的操作，而不是被告知。inline 因为这是一次性的顿悟，看完就过去了，不需要留在侧栏。

prompt: UTF-8 编码和 emoji 那些字符长度的坑
sketch: 一个输入框，用户随便打字或粘 emoji。下面同一串文本用四种方式切分并并排显示：UTF-16 码元（.length）、码点（[...str]）、字素簇（Intl.Segmenter）、UTF-8 字节。每种切分下面标出份数。打一个 👨‍👩‍👧 进去，四行分别显示 8 / 5 / 1 / 25，切分块用颜色对齐让人看出一个字素由哪几个码点、哪几个字节拼成。点任一块显示它的十六进制。
why: 没有任何解释比用户自己粘一个家庭 emoji、看见 .length 是 8 更有说服力。四行对齐是关键——差异必须同屏可比。Intl.Segmenter 是浏览器原生 API，可用。

prompt: 时区和夏令时怎么老出问题
sketch: 一条横向时间轴，上面是 UTC 刻度，下面是用户选的两个时区各一条本地时刻带。拖动时间轴，两条带同步滑。在 DST 切换日，其中一条带上会出现一个视觉缺口（不存在的一小时）或一段重叠阴影（重复的一小时）——用户把游标拖进缺口，右边显示 new Date('2026-03-08T02:30') 在这个时区的实际解析结果和它为什么诡异。可以增删时区行做多方会议时间对照。
why: DST 的两个坑（缺失的一小时、重复的一小时）在时间轴上就是一个洞和一段重影，拖游标进去撞到它，比读文档强一个量级。canvas 因为排会议时区表是会存下来反复用的。

prompt: 大 O 是啥意思，n log n 和 n² 差多少
sketch: 一张对数可选的坐标图，画着 O(1)/O(log n)/O(n)/O(n log n)/O(n²)/O(2ⁿ) 六条线。底部一个 n 滑块，从 10 拖到 1,000,000，右边表格实时显示每条在当前 n 下的操作数和「按每秒一亿次算」折成的耗时（纳秒 / 秒 / 年）。用户拖到十万时 O(n²) 那行跳到「几小时」，2ⁿ 早已是天文数字并被标成溢出。可以勾选只比较两条并显示比值。
why: 复杂度的直觉全在「n 变大时的转折点」，滑块是唯一能表达这件事的控件；折算成时间单位比抽象操作数更扎心。either 是因为它既可以是一次性回答，也常被留着当参照表。

prompt: 讲讲哈希表冲突是怎么处理的
sketch: 一排桶（默认 8 个），用户在输入框敲任意字符串按回车插入，卡片显示 hash → 取模 → 落到几号桶的动画。冲突时按选中的策略演示：链地址法长出一条链，开放寻址则用小箭头一格格往后探测并留下探测路径。顶部一个「桶数」滑块和一个装载因子指示条，拖大桶数触发一次 rehash 全量重排动画。删除某个键时，开放寻址下会看到墓碑标记，以及为什么不能直接置空。
why: 墓碑这件事只有在用户自己删了一个键、再查询后面那个键查不到时才会震撼。手打字符串插入让哈希落点是真随机而非编排好的，冲突自然会发生。canvas 因为要连续插十几个才看得到装载因子上升和 rehash。

prompt: z-index 设了 9999 还是被挡住，为啥
sketch: 左边一棵 DOM 树，每个节点可以点开设置 position / z-index / opacity / transform / filter / will-change。任何一项让节点成为层叠上下文时，该节点在树上被套一个虚线框并标注是哪个属性造成的。右边是按真实层叠顺序排的层列表和一个小预览。用户给某个祖先加 opacity: .99，它的子树立刻被虚线框收编，子节点的 z-index: 9999 在右边层列表里当场掉到那个框内部——挡住它的元素还在上面。底部一个按钮把当前这棵树的状态发回聊天问「我的实际页面里是不是也是这个原因」。
why: 层叠上下文的杀手是「祖先的某个无关属性把你的 z-index 关进了盒子里」，必须让用户亲手给祖先加 opacity 才会信。这也是少数几个玩具会到边界的场景——它解释不了用户真实页面，所以给一个 chat 按钮把状态交回对话，这是唯一值得配 chat 的位置。

prompt: 我 package.json 里这堆依赖，哪些是重复的
sketch: 读 package.json 和 lock 文件，画成一张可拖的依赖图：直接依赖是实心节点，传递依赖是空心。同一个包出现多个版本时，那几个节点被红环圈在一起并标出各自版本和引入路径。用户点任一节点，图只保留从根到它的所有路径（可以看到是谁把这个版本拖进来的）。顶部滑块「深度」限制展开层数，避免图爆炸。
why: lock 文件是纯数据，浏览器里解析完全靠谱，不需要执行 npm。价值在于这是用户自己的项目——「哪个包把 lodash 3 拖进来的」这种问题只有对着真实文件才有意义。canvas 因为依赖图是要来回点、放着慢慢看的。

prompt: 贝叶斯那个假阳性的事儿，我总觉得反直觉
sketch: 一个 100×100 的点阵代表一万人。三个滑块：患病率、灵敏度、特异度。点阵按四色分区：真阳、假阳、真阴、假阴，拖滑块时色块面积连续变形。右边只显示一句话和一个大数字：「检测阳性中真患病的比例」。把患病率从 1% 拖到 0.1%，用户会看到假阳色块淹没真阳色块，那个大数字从 16% 掉到 2%——而灵敏度那个滑块一动不动。
why: 基础率谬误的全部要害是「灵敏度 99% 但答案还是 2%」，让人拖着患病率滑块看假阳区膨胀，比任何公式推导都直接。点阵是面积编码，不是图表——面积是可以被眼睛直接相除的。

prompt: 地图上格陵兰真有那么大吗
sketch: 一张世界地图，顶部切换墨卡托 / 等积 / 罗宾逊等几种投影，切换时国家轮廓做形变过渡。用户可以抓起任意国家的轮廓在地图上拖动，它随纬度实时缩放——把格陵兰拖到赤道，它缩成非洲一角那么大。地图上叠一层可开关的 Tissot 变形椭圆网格，墨卡托下高纬的圆胀成巨球，等积投影下全是等面积的椭圆。
why: 「拖动一个国家跨纬度看它缩水」是这个题目唯一正确的交互——静态对比图人人见过却记不住，手上的拖拽才留得下印象。canvas 因为要横向铺开且会反复玩。

prompt: 为什么钢琴要用十二平均律，跟纯律差在哪
sketch: 一个八度的键盘，点键发声（Web Audio）。每个键上方有两条并排的小竖条：纯律频率和平均律频率，差值以音分标出。用户按住两个键弹和弦，卡片显示两种律制下的拍频，并有一个「A/B」开关直接切换整个键盘的调律——同一个大三和弦切过去，耳朵听得出平均律的三度在轻微打拍。再加一个「转调」滑块，纯律下转到远关系调时某些音程的音分偏差条会红得触目惊心。
why: 这是必须用耳朵而不是眼睛的概念，A/B 切换调律听同一个和弦就是全部教学。Web Audio 是浏览器原生的，可用。canvas 因为要持续弹、要键盘有横向空间。

prompt: 色值那些 hex、hsl、oklch 换来换去我没概念
sketch: 一个大色板加三套滑块（RGB / HSL / OKLCH），拖任一套另两套同步跟随。关键动作：把 HSL 的 L 固定在 50%，拖 H 转一圈，色板下方的「感知亮度」条剧烈起伏（黄很亮、蓝很暗）；换成 OKLCH 把 L 固定拖 H，那条几乎是平的。旁边一列用当前颜色渲染的真实 UI 小样（按钮、文字块）并实时算对白/对黑的对比度，低于 4.5 时打叉。sRGB 色域外的 OKLCH 值在色板上打斜纹。
why: 「HSL 的 L 不是你以为的亮度」这件事，只有在固定 L 转色相、看着感知亮度条起伏时才会被真的接受。对比度小样把它和实际工作接上。canvas 因为调色板是会存下来当项目参照的。

prompt: generator 的 yield 是怎么暂停又回来的
sketch: 左边一段生成器函数源码，当前暂停在哪一行用高亮条标出。右边是调用方，有 next() / next(值) / return() / throw() 四个按钮。点 next() 高亮条从当前 yield 跑到下一个 yield，右边收到 {value, done}；在 next 的输入框里填个值再点，那个值会以气泡形式飞回左边、落在 yield 表达式的位置上——这是最反直觉的一步。点 throw() 看异常从 yield 处抛出并被函数内的 try/catch 接住。
why: generator 最难的不是「暂停」而是「next 的参数变成 yield 的返回值」这个反向数据流，只有把它做成一个从右往左飞的气泡才讲得清。inline 因为这是一次性搞懂的机制。

prompt: this 到底指向啥，我每次都得试
sketch: 一个对象结构图，里面有普通方法、箭头函数、嵌套函数。下面一排调用方式按钮：obj.m()、取出来单独调、call/apply（可填 thisArg）、new、作为回调传给 setTimeout。点任一种，图上会有一根箭头从被调用的函数指到它此刻的 this（对象 / undefined / window / 新实例），并在旁边一行字说明是哪条规则赢了。把普通方法切成箭头函数的开关一拨，那根箭头立刻改指向定义时的外层——嵌套那个的行为反转最明显。
why: this 的规则是一张优先级表，但人记不住表；把「调用方式」做成按钮、把 this 做成一根会改指向的箭头，规则就变成了可枚举的手感。箭头函数开关放在旁边，才能对照出「定义时」和「调用时」的区别。

prompt: 做个能弹的钢琴
sketch: Two-octave keyboard, white keys as flex children with black keys absolutely positioned in a relative wrapper (never fixed). Sound is 3 detuned OscillatorNodes per key (1x sine + 2x/3x triangle at -12/-18dB) into a per-voice GainNode with 8ms attack and exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001) decay whose length scales with pitch — high notes die fast, bass rings. All voices sum into one master gain (0.2) so ten held keys don't clip. Context is created inside the first pointerdown, never at mount, and resume()d if suspended. Computer-keyboard row ASDFGHJ mapped and shown as tiny glyphs on the keys. Sustain on spacebar. Octave shift buttons. localStorage remembers octave + volume. Container measured with ResizeObserver: below ~420px it drops to one octave rather than shrinking keys to unplayable slivers. Unmount closes the AudioContext.
why: The single card the commissioner named first, and the one that proves oscillator-only synthesis is good enough. Canvas because a piano is something you come back to, and the octave/volume choice must survive a reload.

prompt: 节拍器，我练琴用
sketch: BPM 40-240 via a draggable dial plus tap-tempo (median of last 5 taps, outliers dropped). CRITICAL: scheduling is a 25ms setInterval lookahead loop that queues clicks at absolute audioCtx.currentTime + n*(60/bpm) — never one setInterval per beat, which drifts audibly inside 30 seconds. Click = 1kHz (downbeat 1.5kHz) square burst, 30ms, ramped not gated. Time signature 2/4 3/4 4/4 6/8; the beat dots pulse via requestAnimationFrame reading currentTime, so the visual is locked to the audio clock rather than to React state. localStorage keeps bpm/signature. AUTOPLAY: on mount it silently runs at the saved BPM with the dots pulsing and the dial breathing, so the card is visibly alive; the first click anywhere unmutes it.
why: Named explicitly, and it is the card where the naive implementation is provably wrong — the lookahead scheduler is the whole value. Canvas: a practice tool is reopened daily with your tempo intact.

prompt: 给我个简谱，能点着听那种
sketch: 简谱 rendered as pure styled text — digits 1-7, dots above/below for octave, underlines for eighth/sixteenth (border-bottom, stacked), dashes for held beats. No library, because none is needed and none would give clickable notes. Each note is a <span> you can click to hear it alone; a play button walks the phrase with a highlight that slides continuously (the skill forbids jump cuts) while a shared oscillator voice plays it. Key selector (1=C, 1=F...) transposes by semitone offset. A textarea lets you type/paste 简谱 in plain text and it renders live — that is the whole editing story, no note palette. Saves the current piece and a small library to localStorage; a 保存到工作区 button writes the text via $dsh/fs.writeFile so a piece can outlive the browser profile.
why: 简谱 is the cheapest possible sound-making notation — it is text with underlines — so it delivers the audio ask at near-zero risk. fs makes the library real rather than trapped in localStorage.

prompt: 五线谱认音练习
sketch: Hand-drawn SVG staff: five lines, treble/bass clef as a path, ledger lines computed from staff position, notehead as a rotated <ellipse> with a stem. Deliberately NOT vexflow — its esm.sh entry drags in six font modules and draws to a canvas you'd then have to hit-test, whereas SVG gives per-note onClick and a CSS-animated playhead for free. Quiz loop: a note appears, you name it by clicking a piano strip below; right answer plays the pitch and the note slides off, wrong answer shakes it and plays a minor second. Tracks streak + per-note accuracy in localStorage and shows which notes you keep missing. AUTOPLAY: answers itself at ~1.2s intervals with a soft cursor dot moving to the key it picks, occasionally missing on purpose so the wrong-answer state gets demoed too.
why: Covers 五线谱-that-makes-sound, and the note-reading drill is the reason anyone opens a staff twice. The deliberate rejection of vexflow is a real engineering call, not laziness.

prompt: 我有个 mid 文件想看看里面是什么
sketch: Drop zone + file picker — NOT $dsh/fs, because readFile returns a string and a .mid is binary; this is the constraint that shapes the card. File.arrayBuffer() into midi-file (small, esm.sh-verified) → track list with instrument names, note counts, tempo map, duration. Piano-roll view in SVG: time on x, pitch on y, one rect per note, tracks colour-coded, horizontally scrollable in its own overflow container so the panel never scrolls sideways. Play back with a pool of oscillator voices scheduled ahead on currentTime, playhead line moving via rAF; per-track mute/solo. 导出简谱 button writes a transcription of the selected melody track through $dsh/fs.writeFile.
why: The MIDI parser ask, framed around the real limitation instead of into it. The piano roll is what makes a parser worth looking at rather than a JSON dump.

prompt: 连我的 midi 键盘试试
sketch: navigator.requestMIDIAccess is feature-detected first and only called from an explicit 连接设备 button — it triggers a browser permission prompt, so it can never happen on mount. Three honest states: unsupported (shows the computer-keyboard fallback and says why), denied (same fallback, no scolding), connected (device name, live velocity-sensitive keyboard where velocity maps to gain, plus a scrolling event log of note-on/off/CC). The card is fully playable via ASDFGHJ in every state, so a denied prompt costs the user nothing. onstatechange handles unplugging mid-session. Listener and context both torn down on unmount.
why: Web MIDI is genuinely available but permission-gated, and this is the one card where that prompt is the point rather than an obstacle. The three-state design is the whole deliverable.

prompt: 和弦是怎么回事，听听区别
sketch: A row of chord chips — 大三 小三 增 减 属七 大七 — click one and it arpeggiates then sustains, with the interval structure drawn as dots on a mini keyboard underneath and the semitone gaps labelled (4+3, 3+4, ...). A root selector transposes everything. One shared oscillator voice bank, context created on the first chip click. Deliberately small: no staff, no progression builder, no save.
why: Inline is right by the skill's own lifetime rule — this is one step of a conversation about intervals, read once and scrolled past. It also demonstrates that audio cards don't all have to be canvases.

prompt: 来个打节奏的游戏
sketch: Four lanes, notes falling to a hit line, judged against audioCtx.currentTime rather than rAF timestamps so scoring matches what you hear. Perfect/Good/Miss windows at 40/90ms; hits play a pitched click layered over the backing pattern, misses duck the music briefly. Combo counter with a scale-pop that respects prefers-reduced-motion. Charts are plain arrays of [time, lane] generated from a seeded pattern so a given song is always the same. High score + best combo in localStorage. AUTOPLAY: a perfect-play ghost clears the first ~10 seconds with hit flashes and a climbing combo, badge visible; any keypress hands control over instantly, mid-song, and the ghost fades rather than cutting.
why: The audio ask and the games ask are the same card here, and rhythm is the genre where the currentTime-vs-rAF distinction is not pedantry — it is whether the game feels fair.

prompt: 做个贪吃蛇
sketch: Grid on a single <canvas> sized to the container via ResizeObserver (320-720px panel), fixed logical grid, devicePixelRatio-aware. Snake moves on a tick that speeds up with length; each pellet plays a rising pentatonic step so eating a long chain sounds like a scale — the audio is the score, which is the trick that makes a snake worth building here. Death is a descending minor third. Arrow keys and WASD, plus swipe on the canvas for touch. High score in localStorage. AUTOPLAY: a pathfinding bot (BFS to pellet, with a tail-safety check so it doesn't demo itself into a wall in the first eight seconds) plays a clean run with the pentatonic climbing; any arrow key takes over the live snake without resetting the board.
why: The canonical demo game, and the autoplay is genuinely good here because a competent snake bot is short and looks impressive. Pellet-as-note ties it to the audio brief instead of being a generic filler game.

sketch: Standard 4x4, but with motion/react layout animations so tiles slide and merge continuously rather than snapping — the skill explicitly forbids jump cuts and this is where it shows. Merge plays a tone whose pitch rises with the tile's exponent, so a big merge chain is audibly satisfying. Undo one step. Board + best score persisted to localStorage so a reload resumes mid-game. AUTOPLAY: an expectimax-lite bot (depth 2, corner-weighted heuristic) plays about one move per 400ms, reliably reaching 256-512 inside ten seconds with a steady stream of merge tones; arrow keys take over the position as-is.
why: Fits a narrow panel perfectly, the bot is short and looks smart, and pitch-per-exponent is the cheapest possible way to make a silent puzzle game feel alive.

prompt: 扫雷
sketch: Difficulty presets sized to fit the panel width (9x9 / 16x16 with scroll). First click is always safe — mines are placed after it. Flood-fill reveal animates outward from the click as a wave with a soft tick per ring rather than all at once, which is both prettier and the reason the card has sound at all. Right-click / long-press to flag. Timer, mine counter, best time per difficulty in localStorage. AUTOPLAY: a constraint-solver bot performs only provably-safe deductions and highlights the cell it is reasoning about with the two neighbours that justify it — so the demo teaches the game rather than just clicking fast; it pauses visibly when it needs a guess.
why: The autoplay is the standout: showing the deduction is far more compelling in a ten-second demo than showing a solved board, and it is a real algorithm rather than a scripted animation.

prompt: 记忆力翻牌游戏
sketch: Pairs matched by SOUND, not by picture: each card holds a short timbre (a chord, a rhythm, a bell) and flipping plays it — so this is a memory game you play with your ears, which is the reason it exists rather than being the hundredth emoji-matching grid. Cards flip with a real 3D rotateY on a preserve-3d wrapper. Grid columns from container width, not viewport. Moves/time tracked, best per size in localStorage. Falls back gracefully to symbols on the card faces if the AudioContext never resumes, so a muted card is still playable. AUTOPLAY: plays with perfect memory but human pacing — flips a new card, then goes straight to its known partner, so the whole board clears in about eight seconds.
why: Turns the most generic game request into something that could only exist with audio, and it degrades honestly if sound is blocked.

prompt: 跟我玩个猜歌的游戏
sketch: Plays the first N notes of a melody with oscillator voices and you guess the title; each wrong guess buys one more note. The melody bank is a small hardcoded array of public-domain tunes as [midi, duration] pairs — no network, no samples, so it always works. Score is 'how few notes did you need'. $dsh/ai generates the multiple-choice distractors and a one-line hint on demand (single-turn, which is exactly what streamText supports), with a plain fallback list if the stream fails. History and best score in localStorage. AUTOPLAY: cycles a demo round — notes revealing one at a time, options highlighting, a correct answer landing — and loops.
why: Uses $dsh/ai for the one thing it is actually good at here (generating plausible wrong answers and a hint) while keeping the game fully functional if the model call fails, which is the right dependency shape for a single-turn API.

prompt: 练一下音准，我唱一个音你告诉我准不准
sketch: getUserMedia microphone (explicit button, and the permission denial state is a designed screen, not a crash) into an AnalyserNode; pitch detected by autocorrelation on the time-domain buffer — ~40 lines, no library, far more reliable than picking the FFT peak for voice. Shows the detected note, the cents deviation as a needle that damps rather than jitters, and a target note you can set from a piano strip. A 持续音 reference drone from an oscillator so you can tune against it. Session history of how flat/sharp you were per note in localStorage.
why: The only card here that uses audio INPUT without needing a MIDI device, and autocorrelation-over-FFT is a real correctness call that a naive implementation gets wrong.

prompt: 鼓机，我想编个循环
sketch: 16-step grid x 5 tracks (kick sine sweeping 150->50Hz, snare noise burst through a bandpass, closed/open hat filtered noise, clap = three offset noise bursts) — every sound synthesised, zero samples, so nothing loads from the network. Same 25ms lookahead scheduler as the metronome; the step cursor is driven off currentTime via rAF. Swing slider, per-track volume, BPM. Patterns saved to localStorage and exportable as JSON through $dsh/fs.writeFile. AUTOPLAY: mounts with a preloaded groove already running, steps lighting up, silent until the first gesture then it unmutes mid-loop — which is precisely the AudioContext workaround turned into a feature.
why: Best demonstration that pure WebAudio synthesis beats sample loading in this environment, and its autoplay is the cleanest expression of the visual-first, unmute-on-gesture pattern.

prompt: 打砖块
sketch: Paddle follows the pointer with a little lag so it feels weighted; ball physics with angle depending on where it hits the paddle. Each brick row is a scale degree, so clearing a wall bottom-to-top plays an ascending run — audio again doing the work of feedback. Particle burst on break drawn into the same canvas (never document.body — the skill's fullscreen-canvas trap). Lives, levels, high score in localStorage. AUTOPLAY: the paddle tracks the ball's predicted landing point with a deliberate 6% error so it looks played rather than solved, clears a visible chunk of wall in ten seconds; taking the mouse over the canvas hands control back immediately and pauses one beat first so the ball isn't dropped at the moment of handoff.
why: The handoff detail is the thing most autoplay implementations get wrong — control transfer that immediately loses is a bad demo. Scale-per-row keeps it inside the audio brief.

prompt: 能不能把我这个项目做成一个小游戏
sketch: Reads the workspace with $dsh/fs.readdir/readFile — file names, extensions, directory depth — and builds a typing/collect game out of the actual file tree: real filenames fall, you type them, each correct keystroke plays a note stepping through a scale so typing sounds like playing. Directories are bosses. Falls back to a built-in word list if readdir is denied under Read Only mode, and says so in one line rather than erroring. Score and per-run stats in localStorage; a 分享战绩 button uses $dsh/chat.sendMessage to post a plain sentence the user would plausibly type ('我这一局打了 1200 分'), never a JSON payload.
why: The one intent that could only exist in this harness — the game's content IS the user's repo. It also exercises fs, chat, the sandbox-denied path, and audio in a single card without any of them being decoration.

prompt: 这个项目里到底有多少代码？给我看看分布
sketch: Canvas 递归 readdir 整个 workspace，边走边渲染：左侧是随遍历深度逐层展开的树，右侧是按扩展名聚合的体积条形图（recharts），底部一行「已扫描 N 个目录 / M 个文件」随遍历自增。点任一文件用 readFile 拉出来在下方只读预览。node_modules/.git 默认折叠但可展开——不硬性排除，只是懒加载。
why: 这是最能压这个媒介的一类：readdir 是 N 次异步往返，如果等全部走完再渲染，用户面对的是几十秒空白。它成立的关键是把「遍历」本身当成渲染流——每返回一层就 setState 一次，进度是内容而不是 spinner。反面是把整棵树 await 完再画，那就必然散架。size 字段在 DirEntry 里现成，不用为体积再 readFile。

prompt: 帮我盯着 package.json，我改依赖的时候你这边跟着变
sketch: 极简 canvas：一列依赖名 + 版本，setInterval 每 2 秒 readFile('package.json') 重读，内容 hash 不变就什么都不做，变了则 diff 出新增/删除/改版本三类，用 state-success / state-error / state-warn 三色在行首打一个点，新变化的行做一次 3 秒淡出的高亮。顶部只有一行「上次变化：xx 秒前」。
why: 「定时自更新」唯一站得住的形态：底层东西真的在变。要点是 diff 而非重绘——每 2 秒整表重画会让用户永远抓不住变化点，而 hash 短路 + 只高亮变动行，才让轮询变成信息。必须在 unmount 清 interval（dice.ui4a.tsx 里那个 timers.current.forEach(clearInterval) 就是范本）。

prompt: 我想给这个项目写个 README，你先问问我想怎么写
sketch: 一条 inline 卡：先 readdir 顶层 + readFile package.json 拿到真实项目名和脚本，然后给出 3 个具体选项卡片（「面向用户的介绍页」「面向贡献者的开发文档」「一页极简，只有装和跑」），每张卡上写清会包含哪些章节。点击即 sendMessage 发出对应中文回复，卡片进入已选状态并保留高亮。
why: skill 里「用界面提问」那一节的最强版本——选项不是凭空的模板名，而是读了真实文件后给出的、带项目自己名字的具体方案。inline 是对的：这是对话的一步，读一次就滚走。两个半边都要做（sendMessage + 记录已选），只发不记会让回滚看到的卡片像没点过。

prompt: 给我 20 个这个 app 的名字，不满意我还要
sketch: inline 卡，streamText 要 JSON {"names":[{"name":"","why":""}]}，用 partial-json 边解析边把名字一个个落进网格。右下角一个「再来 20 个」，点了把已出现过的全部名字塞进新 prompt 的排除列表里再流一次。每个名字可点，点了 sendMessage「就叫 xxx」。
why: prompt 里明写的「要几个就是要更多」。长流之所以不无聊，是因为落地单位是用户当场就能读能点的名字，不是进度条。单轮限制在这里恰好塑造了设计：没有多轮，所以「排除已见过的」必须自己拼进 prompt——这是模式不是绕路。每个字段都要 ?? 兜底，半个 name 到手就 .toUpperCase() 会当场把卡片打没。

prompt: 把我这堆 markdown 笔记整理成一个能翻的东西
sketch: canvas 主文件 + canvases/notes/{list,reader,search}.tsx 三个子页。主文件只管 readdir 找出所有 .md、维护当前页和滚动位置，写进 localStorage('notes-canvas-v1')。list 页是文件列表带字数；reader 页 readFile 单篇渲染；search 页在已读过的内容里做纯前端子串匹配，点结果跳 reader 并定位。顶部三个 tab，切换不重新扫盘。
why: 子页导航能成立的前提是「回来时还在原处」——canvas 是 preserveState={false}，所以当前页、滚动、搜索词必须落 localStorage，否则模型下次改这个文件，用户就被弹回第一页。tarot 那个已经证明 canvases/<id>/ 拆文件是通的（deck.ts）。搜索只在已加载内容里做是诚实的设计，不是偷懒：没有 ripgrep，假装全库搜索会给出静默不全的结果。

prompt: 这周的开销我念给你，你记一下
sketch: canvas：上面一个输入框接自然语言（「今天中午 32 打车 18」），streamText 解析成 JSON {items:[{name,amount,category}]} 追加进账本；下面是按类目的环形图和明细表。全部数据 localStorage('ledger-v1')，同时提供一个「导出到 expenses.csv」按钮走 writeFile，只读会话下 catch 到 FS_SANDBOX_DENIED 就把按钮变成一行说明而不是报错弹窗。
why: canvas 的定义性用例：十轮之后还想再打开。ai 用在真开放的地方（自由文本→结构化），钱和图表都是纯计算不碰模型。writeFile 的只读降级要当作正常分支写——types 里 FS_SANDBOX_DENIED 是明写的契约，不 catch 就是一个看起来坏掉的按钮。私有状态留在 localStorage、导出才落盘，正好是 skill 里那条分界。

prompt: 这个函数在项目里都谁在用？
sketch: canvas：先 readdir 递归收集所有 .ts/.tsx，然后按批（每批 8 个）readFile 并做正则匹配，边匹配边把命中项追加到结果列表——每行是文件路径 + 行号 + 前后各两行上下文，行号可点展开整段。顶部一个进度条写「已看 37/210 个文件」，可中途取消。
why: 这是「读二十个文件」的真实形态，而且必须诚实：没有 ripgrep，所以这是逐文件正则，会命中注释和字符串里的同名。卡片要把这点写在结果上方一行，而不是假装自己是 LSP。成立的关键是分批 + 增量出结果 + 可取消：一次性 Promise.all 两百个 readFile 既卡又没有中途可看的东西。

prompt: 今天专注一下，帮我看着时间
sketch: 几乎全空的 canvas：面板正中一个巨大的剩余时间，下面一行极小的「专注 / 休息」，再无别的。没有边框没有卡片没有标题（面板已经有标题栏了）。点任意处开始/暂停，长按重置。完成一轮时整块背景做一次极缓的色相位移，不弹窗不撒花。localStorage 记住当前轮次和已完成数。
why: 「故意留白」的正确用法：这是一个用户瞥一眼的常驻仪表，不是一个答案。已有的 pomodoro.ui4a.tsx 是 472 行的反面教材——一个番茄钟不需要 472 行。它成立是因为唯一的信息（还剩多久）被放到了最大，其余全部删掉；它会散架的地方是有人往里加统计图表和成就徽章，那就变回一张被装饰的卡片，正是 skill 明令禁止的那种。

prompt: 对比一下这几个方案，我拿不定主意
sketch: 同一条回复里两块 inline：第一块是可编辑的对比表（行=方案，列=维度，权重可拖），第二块是随权重实时重算的加权得分条形图。两块通过 localStorage('compare-draft') 同一个 key 通信——表格写，图表监听 storage 事件 + 100ms 轮询兜底。图表下方一行「选它」按钮各自 sendMessage。
why: 「一条回复里几张互相关联的卡」唯一能成立的接线方式：没有跨卡片的 React 上下文，共享 state 对象是幻想，共享 key 才是真的。storage 事件同页面不触发，所以必须配一个小间隔轮询兜底——这一条不知道就会得到一个「另一张卡永远不动」的 bug。拆成两块而不是一块，是因为表格要宽、图表要窄，在 320px 面板里堆一起谁都读不了。

prompt: 把这段日志给我理一理，太长了看不动
sketch: canvas：readFile 一个 log 文件，按行切分后用 @tanstack/react-virtual 虚拟滚动几万行。顶部一排等级过滤（error/warn/info）和一个即时正则输入，右侧一条压缩成 2px 宽的全文缩略图，错误行在上面是红色刻度，点刻度直接跳过去。行号常驻，选中行展开成可换行全文。
why: 「上千行」的关键不是虚拟滚动本身，而是给出一个「整体形状」的东西——缩略条让几万行有了地图，否则用户只是在一个更快的滚动条里迷路。readFile 是整文件字符串没有流式，所以超大文件要先看 readdir 给的 size，超过阈值就明说只渲染前 N MB，而不是把浏览器 tab 卡死。过滤必须在虚拟化之上做索引，不是 filter 完重建列表。

prompt: 给我讲讲这个仓库是干嘛的，边讲边给我看代码
sketch: canvas 分上下：上半是 streamText 逐段流出的讲解，下半是一个跟着讲解走的代码窗。做法是先 readFile 几个关键文件（package.json、入口、README）把真实内容塞进 prompt，要求模型输出 JSON {sections:[{title,body,file,lines}]}；每流出一个 section，下半自动 readFile 那个 file 并滚到 lines。用户可以随时点回上一段，流继续但不再抢镜头。
why: 长流保持有趣的最好形态：流出来的每一段都带一个可看的落点。ai 拿到的是真读来的文件内容而不是记忆，所以讲解不会编造文件名——这正是 CLAUDE.md 里反复强调的「你读了不等于卡片读了」的反向用法：模型读来做决策，卡片自己再读来做展示。file/lines 每个字段都可能半截，跳转前必须校验存在再 readFile，否则一次 undefined 路径就把整个卡片 unmount。

prompt: 随便给我出点题，我做一道你出一道，别停
sketch: canvas：一次只显示一道题。答完立刻判定，同时后台已经在 streamText 下一道（始终预取 1 道，所以永远不用等）。每道题的 prompt 里带上最近 5 题的题面和对错，让难度跟着走。顶部只有「已做 N / 正确率 X%」和一个显眼的停止键；停止后停在当前题，不清空。全部进度 localStorage。
why: 「一直生成直到你喊停」的可用版本——无限流的问题从来不是怎么开始而是怎么不烦人：预取一道让等待消失，一次只显示一道让内容不堆积，停止键必须在第一屏而不是列表末尾。单轮无记忆恰好逼出正确设计：自适应难度靠把最近 5 题拼进 prompt，而不是靠一个不存在的会话。卸载时必须置取消标志，否则用户关了面板还在烧 token。

prompt: 这个配置文件我改哪儿能关掉那个功能？
sketch: inline 卡：readFile 配置文件，把它渲染成一棵可折叠的键值树，每个布尔值是一个真开关。用户拨动开关后卡片不立刻写盘，而是显示一个 diff 预览（红绿两行），确认后 writeFile 回去。只读会话下开关变成只读徽章加一行说明。
why: inline 是对的——这是当下这一步，改完就滚走，不是个要回来的地方。写盘前先给 diff 是这个媒介里少有的必需防御：卡片写文件是用户看不见的副作用，没有确认步骤就等于让一次误触改了仓库。渲染的是当场 readFile 的内容而不是模型粘贴的快照，所以文件被别处改过时它是对的。

prompt: 我要挑张照片当封面，你把候选摆出来让我选
sketch: inline 卡：readdir 目标目录、按扩展名筛出图片，做成一个网格——但因为 readFile 只能读文本，格子里放的不是缩略图，而是文件名 + 尺寸(size) + 修改序位，加一行明说「这里看不到图，只能按文件信息选」。点一张 sendMessage「用 xxx.jpg」，卡片保留选中态。
why: 故意选一个媒介做不到的请求，因为它示范了正确的失败方式。readFile 是纯文本，二进制没有路——诚实地说出来并给出仍然有用的东西（文件清单 + 体积 + 点选即回话），远好过用一个 broken 的 网格假装能预览。这类边界卡片的成败全在那一行说明是否在第一屏。

prompt: 帮我把这周聊过的东西整理成一页
sketch: canvas：一个只有输入框和一列条目的极简收集器。用户粘一段话，streamText 抽成 {title, tags[], summary} 追加；条目按 tag 聚合成可折叠分组。没有侧边栏、没有工具栏、没有统计——只有条目和一个「导出 notes.md」。数据 localStorage，导出走 writeFile。
why: 「大部分留白」和「canvas 要活很久」的交集。它成立是因为界面里每一个像素都是用户自己的内容，chrome 只有一个输入框；它会散架的地方是加上搜索框、排序、视图切换这三件套——面板最窄 320px，多一排控件就没有内容的位置了。tags 是流出来的数组，未完成时是 undefined，分组前必须 ?? [] 兜底。

prompt: 这个项目是干嘛的？
sketch: README 首段 + 一侧可展开的目录树，点文件名右侧现读该文件前 40 行。全部 readdir/readFile 在渲染时发生。
why: 打开陌生仓库后几乎必然出现的第一句，任何仓库都成立，且一眼看出卡片读的是真文件而不是模型的快照。

prompt: 帮我看看这个仓库的结构
sketch: 可折叠树，目录来自 readdir 的 type 字段（无需探测），文件带 size 条形，点一下展开子目录。
why: 和上一条同频但更明确要求结构；prose 版必然被压平成缩进文本，交互树是明显更好的答案。

prompt: 这个 cron 表达式啥意思 0 3 * * 1-5
sketch: 五个字段拆成五个可点的段，下面列出未来 10 次触发时间；改任一段实时重算。
why: 新手本来就会顺手问，答案有可调参数，一秒看到「改一下就变」的 payoff，且完全不依赖仓库。

prompt: 月供怎么算的，300 万 30 年 3.1%
sketch: 三个滑块 + 月供数字 + 本息比例饼图，附提前还款开关。
why: prompt.ts 明确点名的场景（有数字就该给控件）；这是最容易让人「oh」的非编码类问题，且传播性强。

prompt: 帮我可视化一下这些数据
sketch: 粘贴的 CSV/JSON 直接解析，recharts 图 + 图表类型切换 + 列选择器。
why: 「可视化」在任何 agent 里都是高频句式；差异点是这里不跑 python、不出 PNG，图是活的、能换维度。

prompt: 这个正则我看不懂
sketch: 分组高亮 + 一个测试输入框，输入即时显示匹配片段和捕获组。
why: 日常提问，静态解释永远不如让他把自己的字符串贴进去试一次。

prompt: 依赖都装了些啥
sketch: 读 package.json，deps/devDeps 分组、搜索框过滤、按名字排序，显示版本区间。
why: 任意 JS 仓库必有的文件，证明 fs 不是靠精心准备的样例；也顺手展示 esm.sh 现拉库无需安装。

prompt: 哪些文件最大
sketch: 递归 readdir 汇总 size，按扩展名着色的条形榜 + 目录下钻。
why: 仓库无关的纯文件事实，任何项目都有结果，不会空手；排行榜天然适合交互。

prompt: 帮我起几个名字
sketch: streamText 流式产出候选卡，带「再来一批」和风格切换（简洁/复古/技术感）。
why: prompt.ts 里的「要几个就是想要更多」原型；用户下一句必然是「再来点」，而卡片已经把这句消掉了。

prompt: 给我推荐点晚饭吃啥
sketch: 输入冰箱里有的东西 → streamText 生成菜谱卡，展开看步骤。
why: 新手随口一问的非工作类问题，答案空间开放，是 streamText 判据的教科书案例（真实产物 recipe-generator 就长这样）。

prompt: 帮我做个番茄钟
sketch: 侧栏计时器，localStorage 存轮次与设置，跨轮次不丢。
why: 最典型的显式「做个工具」请求，也是仓库里真实存在的产物；概率不如前面几条高，因为新手还不知道能这么要。

prompt: 做个待办清单
sketch: 侧栏列表，增删改 + localStorage 持久化，重开对话仍在。
why: 最俗但也最真实的 canvas 触发语；它的价值是让用户第一次意识到面板会一直留着。

prompt: 这两个方案选哪个？
sketch: 2–4 张可点选项卡，点击即 sendMessage 成为下一轮用户消息，选后保留高亮。
why: 决策类提问很常见；把「你想要哪个」从打字变成点击，是 chat 能力最省口舌的自证。

prompt: 做个工具给我用
sketch: 先给一张三选一的提问卡（每项都是能立刻开工的具体东西），点一个才开始建。
why: skill.ts 专门为这句设计；含糊请求用可点选项回问，比 prose 追问少一轮打字，也顺带演示 UI 可作为输入。

prompt: 这个配置文件能不能给我个界面改
sketch: readFile 解析 json/yaml，按字段生成表单，改完 writeFile 回原路径；只读会话捕获失败并直说。
why: 概率不高但杀伤力最大——写回真实文件；也是唯一会自然撞上 sandbox 只读边界的场景，值得让它优雅失败。
